sources.locator: §2.1 (printed pp.181–182 / PDF pp.4–5), §2.3 and Remark 2.5 (printed p.184 / PDF p.7), Proposition 2.6 (printed p.184 / PDF p.7) and proof §5.1 (printed pp.197–198 / PDF pp.20–21)

contents.name: §2.1 configuration sigma algebra generated by count evaluations and its Borel presentation
contents.argument: The source records count-generated configuration measurability for simple point fields. The local lemma proves the exact finite unmarked sorted-list interface by recovering each lexicographic point from count maps.

contents.name: §2.1 Marked point random fields: simple configurations, count-generated sigma algebra, local observables with linear count growth, and the local-convergence topology
contents.argument: The source motivates the local-tame tests and local topology. The assigned item spells out the unmarked finite-intensity domain and proves its own configuration sigma-algebra interface; no marked-space or Palm assertion is imported.

contents.name: §2.3 Poisson random fields and specific entropy: independent Poisson counts and the reference field
contents.argument: The paper states the point-process characterization. The local proof derives cell-piece count laws, restriction independence, and translation invariance for the explicitly constructed unmarked reference.

contents.name: §2.3 equation (2.11): bounded-test variational formula for relative entropy
contents.argument: The local lemma proves the formula for arbitrary probability measures, then proves restriction, product chain, and conditioning monotonicity needed by the spatial items.

contents.name: §2.3 definition (2.12) and Remark 2.5: specific entropy and its supremum over bounded regions
contents.argument: The source records the continuum specific-entropy definition and cube supremum. The assigned proof derives the exact half-open-cube limit and bounded-restriction finiteness used downstream.

contents.name: Proposition 2.6 and proof in §5.1: compactness of bounded specific-entropy levels in a linear-growth local topology
contents.argument: The paper's marked point-field result is related context; the local proof separately establishes compactness and sequential compactness for the declared simple unmarked configuration space and its local-tame topology.

contents.name: Mark spaces, Palm measures, empirical-field large deviations, and Gibbsian extension results
contents.reason: The assigned pair is limited to an unmarked reference, entropy density, local-tame compactness, and information convergence; marked Palm and large-deviation conclusions require additional items and hypotheses outside the reserved inventory.

contents.name: §6 Theorem (6.6): directed L1 convergence of logarithms of finite-subalgebra densities under finite entropy
contents.argument: Nguyen–Zessin provides the directed conditional-density result in its spatial-process setting. The local proof derives it from the stated density formula, entropy chain rule, and uniformly integrable martingale convergence, and records the actual finite-past interface.

contents.name: §6 Theorem (6.26): generalized McMillan theorem for spatial processes with independent increments
contents.argument: The source theorem gives an invariant L1 limit under its (6.15)–(6.18) process assumptions and invokes a spatial ergodic theorem. The local proof supplies the exact unmarked Poisson cube argument, including its full-translation ergodicity step.

contents.name: Assumptions (6.15)–(6.18): spatial automorphisms, sigma-algebras assigned to regions, independent increments, and covariance
contents.argument: These are inspected as the hypotheses of Theorem (6.26); the local reference definition verifies the corresponding cell-product and translation interfaces directly rather than treating a draft label as a proof.
contents.reason: The reference law is constructed and proved from the declared standard-Borel, product-measure, and Poisson-count interfaces on the A page; no spatial-process construction is imported from this inaccessible endpoint.

contents.name: Other spatial-process, lattice, interaction-energy, and point-process applications in §§3–7

alternatives.argument: The complete local proof constructs finite-past conditional densities from the standard-Borel conditional-density formula, identifies their expected log densities by the relative-entropy chain rule, and bounds their entropy by the specific-entropy density. The lifted density martingale is uniformly integrable by the entropy tail bound, hence converges in L1 to the full-past density. The log negative parts have a uniform exponential-tail bound; convergence in probability plus convergence of expected logs yields L1 convergence of both signs, and conditional-expectation contraction proves directed convergence over every larger finite past.

The complete local proof factors the cube density into ordered conditional log densities, approximates its normalized log by averages of the full-past integrable log density, and proves the cube averages converge in L1 using commuting coordinate von Neumann projections and truncation. A quantitative symmetric-difference bound gives integer-shift invariance; overlap cubes and conditional entropy tails transfer the limit to every real translation. Full-translation ergodicity then makes the limit constant, whose mean is the specific entropy density.
